candidates.statement: Every real signed Radon measure of polynomial total-variation growth, Fourier-selfdual for exp(-2pi*i*x*xi), with exact punctured unit gap and nonnegative restriction off Z, equals its origin mass times the integer comb.
proof_assessment: Compact autocorrelation smoothing makes f_epsilon Schwartz and its Fourier transform w_epsilon=sincSquared*|Fourier(phi_epsilon)|^2 nonnegative.
Each w_epsilon is Schwartz and absolutely integrable against polynomial-growth total variation; do not assume bare sincSquared is integrable.
Uniform convergence f_epsilon->triangle on one fixed compact gives integral f_epsilon->nu({0}); exact origin term in integral w_epsilon is nu({0}).
Fatou applies to the positive OFF-LATTICE restriction. It yields integral sincSquared dnu_off=0 even if this extended integral was not previously finite.
Strict positivity of sincSquared off Z forces lattice support. Full distributional selfduality plus integer support implies unit periodicity; compact atom tests give equal weights.
Evenness follows from Fourier squared equals reflection; it is not an extra hypothesis. Negative scalar combs are allowed.
api_gap: P0 HasLinearGrowth is O(R), not polynomial O(R^N).
P0 HasUnitGap removes origin mass; C2 permits it. Do not pass a punctured gap as HasUnitGap.
P0 regularizedTriangle uses ONE normalized bump, whose Fourier multiplier need not be nonnegative. A double convolution/reflection lemma is required.
Use toTemperedDistribution with derived temperate-growth instances; generalize translation/pairing support arguments without pretending polynomial growth is linear.
boundary_controls: c*comb for c positive, zero and negative satisfies exactly the claimed classification.
A lattice-supported weighted comb is not automatically periodic; periodicity uses selfduality.
Derivative-of-atom tempered distributions are excluded by the order-zero measure premise.
For mu=sum_n (n+1/2)^2 delta_(n+1/2), polynomial mass growth holds while bare integral sincSquared dmu diverges; P0's linear-growth dominated-convergence shortcut is unavailable.
candidates.native_authority: No actual native positive selfdual sharp-gap measure is constructed.

candidates.tested_identity: P_epsilon-N_epsilon = D_epsilon + integral f_epsilon dnu - nu({0})
candidates.identity_assessment: Correct, including the sign of D=<Fourier(nu)-nu,f> and the origin subtraction; w_epsilon(0)=1 and w_epsilon(n)=0 at every nonzero integer.
candidates.error: The first displayed inequality has no upper restriction on epsilon. Its replacement of the smoothing-support interval [-1-epsilon,1+epsilon] by [-2,2] is invalid when epsilon>1.

repair_proposals.statement: Keep the original [-2,2] cost and explicitly require 0<=epsilon<=1 (or the natural nonvacuous 0<epsilon<=1). Do not silently add this to the source proposal.
For general epsilon>=0 replace epsilon*TV([-2,2]) by epsilon*TV([-1-epsilon,1+epsilon]).

derivation: Triangle is 1-Lipschitz, psi is nonnegative mass one and supported in [-epsilon,epsilon], so |f_epsilon-triangle|<=epsilon.
The difference vanishes outside [-1-epsilon,1+epsilon]. Integrating against variation gives the general smoothing cost.
Punctured gap (-a,a) makes |integral triangle dnu - nu({0})| <= (1-a)*TV([-1,1]).
The exact identity and triangle inequality then yield the repaired first bound.
second_bound_assessment: R>=1 and epsilon<=1/(2*pi*R) already force epsilon<1, so the stated second bound avoids the first-bound defect.
From even nonnegative phi and support(phi*reflection(phi)) subset [-epsilon,epsilon], positivity rules out phi support beyond [-epsilon/2,epsilon/2].
P0 sincSquared_lower_on_signedBudgetRegion gives sincSquared>=4*d^2/(pi^2*R^2); multiplying gives the stated d^2/(pi^2*R^2) coefficient.
Alternatively prove the half-Fourier lower bound from an explicitly constructed bump supported in [-epsilon/2,epsilon/2], as an explicit regularizer definition, not an unannounced new assumption.
candidates.native_rate_correction: An upper bound E_T<=exp(o(T)) for nonnegative E_T yields log(1+E_T)=o(T), not literal E_T=exp(o(T)) without lower control. E_T=exp(-T), or E_T=0, falsifies the latter literal reading.
native_obligations_open: Construct a genuine order-zero measure from the unchanged physical j/Pj source.
Prove independent tested Fourier-defect estimates rather than repackage high-mask energy.
Track negative mass, gap deficit, local variation, b_T, c_T and the R_T^2/d_T^2 observation loss in the actual same-source theorem.
Discharge native J5.2 and all actual observation identities; no NativeCandidate structure may hide these as solved fields.

candidates.statement: A fixed polynomial-growth lattice-supported signed Radon correction cannot make a nonzero positive off-lattice, punctured-unit-gapped component Fourier-selfdual while preserving those conditions.
proof_assessment: For lattice eta, integral w_epsilon deta=eta({0}) exactly; compact regularizer convergence gives integral f_epsilon deta->eta({0}).
For positive off-lattice nonzero lambda with a unit gap, integral f_epsilon dlambda->0, while Fatou gives liminf integral w_epsilon dlambda>=integral sincSquared dlambda>0 (possibly infinity).
Full selfduality of lambda+eta would equate the two tested pairings for every shrinking epsilon, a contradiction.
This direct proof avoids needing the complete periodic-weight conclusion of C2, though C2 also implies the obstruction.
candidates.quantifier_limit: The correction eta is one fixed order-zero measure and selfduality is an equality of distributions, or at least all shrinking regularized tests. This is not a claim about one finite scalar test.
candidates.finite_stage_countercontrol: For any regularizer with f_epsilon(1)>0, eta=c*delta_1 has D_eta=-c*f_epsilon(1); choose c to cancel a chosen component's D_epsilon exactly for that single test. The unit open gap is retained. Such a correction does not establish full selfduality.
candidates.excluded: Lattice delta derivatives, epsilon-dependent corrections and uncontrolled limiting total variation require separate analysis.
